summary: USB-C dock triggers asymmetric routing and Okta SSO timeouts when Wi-Fi + Ethernet active
environment: Office - SF; employee laptops (Windows 11 + macOS 13); corp-wireguard-prod; corp-dhcp/dns
description: Multiple engineers reported inability to authenticate to Okta-backed internal apps while connected to the USB-C dock at SF office. Symptoms: repeated SSO timeouts or hanging at 'Signing in...' in browser, intermittent 502/524 errors in internal services. Disconnecting the dock (relying on laptop Wi-Fi only) restores SSO and internal app connectivity immediately. Issue started 2026-03-09 after a recent batch of Dell TB4 docks were deployed to hot-desks. This ticket centralizes investigation and mitigation notes.
impact: ~14 employees across two floors affected intermittently. Productivity impact: cannot sign in to internal apps (Confluence, Jira, internal admin UIs). No customer-facing outage. Roll-based fix required for broader fleet if regression replicates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect Windows 11 laptop to USB-C TB4 dock (ethernet out) while Wi-Fi remains connected to corp-wifi
2) Launch WireGuard-based corp VPN client (auto-start) or ensure it is active
3) Open browser and navigate to any Okta-protected internal application (e.g., https://internal.redwood.test)
4) Observe SSO hanging on 'Redirecting to Okta...' or receive a TLS timeout; unplug dock or disable Ethernet adapter -> SSO completes within 1–3s
5) Reconnect dock -> problem returns within seconds
observed_behavior: When dock connected, initial TCP SYN/handshake to Okta completes but TLS handshake stalls and browser reports timeout. WireGuard client logs show repeated handshake timeouts. Packet capture from client shows SYNs originating from expected private IP but server responses (SYN-ACK) are received on a different interface or not at all; many RSTs and retransmits observed. DNS queries for internal hostnames sometimes resolve to public IPs while on the docked path due to suffix/order issues.
expected_behavior: With dock connected and VPN up, SSO and internal apps should authenticate normally regardless of Wi-Fi/Ethernet order. Network stack should prefer corporate route for traffic destined to Okta/internal services and not produce asymmetric routing.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-09 16:10 - Initial reports from #internal-support: SSO failures concentrated on users docked at SF hotdesks. Reporter test reproduces with dock A02.
Checked WireGuard server logs: no upstream errors; saw multiple handshake attempts from same client IPs but no established session when dock connected.

Captured packets at client and observed mismatched destination IPs for responses (asymmetric path). Hypothesis: dock provides a small NAT/bridge that creates a secondary default route; Windows interface metrics prefer Wi-Fi or dock unpredictably leading to source IP selection mismatch.

Test: disabled Wi-Fi, authenticated successfully via Ethernet while docked. Re-enabled Wi-Fi, problem returned. Setting Ethernet interface metric lower than Wi-Fi (manual) made problem disappear for test machine.

Reproduced on macOS laptop: when dock created additional virtual interface (bridge 192.168.50.0/24), DNS suffix order changed and curl to internal services went to public IP; adjusting service order fixed immediately.

Checked recent hardware provisioning: new Dell TB4 docks firmware v1.3.2 deployed 2026-03-07. Vendor release notes mention 'alternate interface mode' which can surface as a bridge device on host. Suspect firmware interacts poorly with OS metric assignment.

SRE ran controlled pcap in lab: when laptop source IP differs from interface used to receive server replies, TCP handshake fails because server replies are NATed out a different public IP; Okta drops incomplete TLS sessions.
Related to INT-33109 (dns-suffix-order) - cross-referenced for DNS suffix behavior but root cause is multi-homing and source IP mismatch.
actions_taken: Immediate mitigation (2026-03-10): Posted dispatcher KB in #internal-support instructing affected users to either unplug dock or disable 'Ethernet (Dock)' adapter until fix applied.

Temporary fleet mitigation (2026-03-11): Endpoint team rolled out Group Policy to set interface metric precedence on Windows: Ethernet (Dock) metric forced to 15, Wi-Fi metric 25 for corporate SSID. Rollout targeted SF office first (approx. 120 devices).
macOS mitigation (2026-03-11): Pushed login script via Jamf to set network service order to prefer Ethernet when dock present; script also removes bridge service created by docks where possible.
Coordinated with vendor (Dell) to request firmware build that changes bridge behavior and to confirm TB4 firmware backport is possible. Vendor acknowledged and opened case DELL-INC-88792.
Network team added a temporary WireGuard server-side rule to accept handshakes where payloads show mixed source IPs (rate-limited) to reduce false negatives while endpoint mitigations propagate.
Manual validation: 12 test users verified fix and reported restored SSO flows. No further regressions observed after GP/Jamf policies applied.
Follow-up ticket created to automate interface metric enforcement for all corporate images (INT-928004).
resolution: Mitigated by enforcing interface metric order on Windows via GPO and network service order script for macOS. Endpoint team to bake metric changes into golden images. Dell provided firmware work item; vendor will release patch v1.3.3 addressing bridge mode. Closing this incident as 'Resolved' after 48h with no recurrence in SF office. Permanent follow-ups: INT-928004 (image changes), work with vendor DELL-INC-88792 for firmware QA and wide deployment.
